name: Bianca Spencer
life: “I still remember folding fuel money inside a birthday card.” Saturday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Bianca usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I can pay toward fuel but can't say it in front of my kids. We made a little envelope in the glove box.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Bianca has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Bianca squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
personality: Bianca is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Bianca is concerned.
family: Malcolm Lund is Bianca’s second cousin. Bianca makes the call. Malcolm is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *An ordinary mirror*, Malcolm says, “I want to make her a new mirror in the same shape.”
connections: Ellen Randall. The no-smoking driver agrees to handle fuel money out of the rider's children's hearing.

reactions.situation: A driver on the rota asks for petrol money
reactions.response: Bianca agrees what the fuel actually cost and discusses the contribution privately.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Bianca asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.
